note: Adapted from Hill (1927), Memoirs of the National Museum, Melbourne 7; the original combination is Microcerotermes serratus (Froggatt). The measurement table is badly damaged in the OCR and is not transcribed; synonymy, distribution and biology are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Head shape of the soldier varies little within a colony, though head size and outline differ slightly between colonies. The alate is closely related to M. parviceps, which is redder, has slightly larger eyes and much smaller ocelli; the soldier is most closely related to M. boreus.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head slightly longer than wide, sides nearly parallel, posterior margin rounded; anterior margin of the pronotum turned up and the anterolateral angles narrowed, correcting the truncate condition misstated in the original description and figure; antennal joints elongate; head surface with long setae.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head and thorax dark bay; abdomen and pleura a little lighter; postclypeus Sudan brown, distinctly paler than the head; anteclypeus hyaline; labrum yellow; antennae, palpi and legs Dresden brown, coxae, femora and tibiae suffused with darker brown; wings light fuscous. Head small, hemispherical behind the eyes, narrowed to the clypeus and densely setose; labrum narrow at the base, swollen at the sides, apex rounded; clypeus large and strongly convex; eyes small, circular and prominent; ocelli small, broadly oval and well separated from the eyes; antennae 14-jointed, the 3rd joint smallest, the 4th to 12th moniliform and increasing in size, the 13th and 14th about as long as the 12th, the last broadly oval; pronotum densely covered with large setae; wings long and narrow, margins setose, radial sector setose throughout, cubitus with nine to thirteen branches.
